## Purpose and Runtime Entry Points
Open SWE is a deployable software-engineering agent system: it receives work from dashboard, GitHub, Slack, Linear, or schedules; executes durable agent runs; works in isolated environments; and delivers or reviews pull requests. The custom FastAPI application is `agent/webapp.py`, with server startup in `agent/server.py`; LangGraph graph entrypoints are registered through `agent/graphs/agent.py`, `agent/graphs/reviewer.py`, and `agent/graphs/scheduler.py`. `langgraph.json` and `langgraph.desktop.json` define runtime deployment variants.

## Invocation and Thread Lifecycle
Inbound integrations normalize requests into durable threads and invocations. Thread state, access, run views, plans, summaries, and approvals are concentrated in `agent/threads/routes.py`, `agent/threads/runs.py`, and `agent/threads/workflow_approval.py`. Dispatch selects an execution path based on source and task type in `agent/dispatch.py` and `agent/invocation.py`. A thread persists conversation/work context across multiple LangGraph runs; cloud coding threads bind to a persistent sandbox, while read-only review/chat can avoid one.

## Agent Graph Assembly and Guardrails
The principal coding graph plans, investigates, edits, validates, and delivers changes; reviewer, analyzer, and chat graphs specialize for read-only PR work and repository-style learning. Graph composition resides in `agent/graphs/agent.py`, `agent/graphs/reviewer.py`, and `agent/graphs/analyzer.py`. Cross-cutting middleware governs preparation, model selection/fallback, dynamic tool exposure, retries, validation, tracing, plan mode, and push restrictions: `agent/middleware/prepare_run.py`, `agent/middleware/model_selection.py`, `agent/middleware/dynamic_tools.py`, and `agent/middleware/workflow_push_guard.py`. Prompts and tool contracts are versioned as repository resources under `agent/resources/prompts/system/main.md`, `agent/resources/prompts/reviewer/main.md`, and `agent/resources/prompts/tools/`.

## Sandboxed Execution Boundary
Coding execution is isolated behind a provider-neutral sandbox lifecycle. `agent/sandboxes/lifecycle.py` creates, recovers, and manages persistent environments; `agent/sandboxes/repo_prep.py` prepares repositories and workspace setup; `agent/sandboxes/providers/registry.py` selects providers. Supported implementations include LangSmith, Modal, Daytona, Runloop, E2B, and local execution under `agent/sandboxes/providers/`. This boundary protects server-held credentials and avoids silently replacing unreachable sandboxes that may contain uncommitted work.

## Integrations, Delivery, and Automation
GitHub is both an ingress and delivery boundary: webhook handling, authenticated API access, PR context/diffs, comments, checks, and PR operations reside in `agent/github/webhook.py`, `agent/github/pull_requests.py`, and `agent/github/checks.py`. Slack and Linear provide parallel event-driven entry points in `agent/slack/routes.py`, `agent/slack/events.py`, and `agent/linear/webhook.py`. Scheduled automations and CI monitoring flow through `agent/schedules/store.py`, `agent/scheduler.py`, and `agent/baby_sit.py`. The expedited-review subsystem adds opt-in approval/readiness/voting workflows under `agent/expedited_review/`.

## State, Identity, and Observability
PostgreSQL-backed ORM and migrations define durable product state, including analytics, threads/PRs, users, and workspaces: `agent/database/orm.py`, `agent/database/postgres.py`, and `agent/database/migrations/versions/`. Authorization and credential scoping are enforced in `agent/users/authorization.py`, `agent/credential_scope.py`, and `agent/encryption.py`. Analytics uses capture/outbox/worker-style stages in `agent/analytics/capture.py`, `agent/analytics/outbox.py`, and `agent/analytics/worker.py`. LangSmith is the default tracing and sandbox service; MCP integrations are modeled and routed in `agent/mcp/runtime.py` and `agent/mcp/routes.py`.

## Product Surfaces
The browser dashboard is a TypeScript/React Vite application rooted at `ui/src/router.tsx`, with agent-thread streaming UI in `ui/src/features/agents/lib/stream/AgentStreamProvider.tsx` and server proxy boundaries in `ui/server/backend-proxy.ts`. The experimental Electron desktop client launches/supervises a local backend and operates on allowlisted local projects via `desktop/src/main.cts`, `desktop/src/backend-supervisor.cjs`, and `desktop/src/project-store.cts`. Desktop-local agent behavior bridges through `agent/desktop.py` and `agent/desktop_branch.py`.
